results.title: Meet Agent Hub and Agent Builder: One place to build and manage AI agents with shared context
results.content:
Most go-to-market teams running AI agents today have the same problem: the agents are scattered and disconnected. A sales team's prospecting agent is reaching out to a customer the same week a service agent is handling an open complaint from that same account. Neither agent knows what the other is doing. And when leadership asks what their AI investment is actually producing, nobody has a clean answer.

HubSpot is launching Agent Hub and Agent Builder to solve those challenges, available today in public beta for all Professional and Enterprise customers. [...] "The problem isn't managing a single agent in isolation. It's that once you have multiple agents, they become fragmented, all working from different pictures of the customer, or even worse, no picture at all," said Duncan Lennox, Chief Product and Technology Officer at HubSpot. "Agent Hub fixes that. One place to see agent performance, all working together and using shared context. That's what will drive outcomes for go-to-market teams."

### Agent Hub

Agent Hub gives go-to-market teams—marketing, sales, and service—a single home to see and manage every agent running across their business. From one place, teams can: [...] See the live status and performance for every active agent
 Identify agents that haven't been turned on yet and activate them with one click
 Access Agent Builder, HubSpot’s new tool for building and improving custom agents and automations with natural language, and Agent Marketplace without leaving Agent Hub
 Manage agent outcomes organized by go-to-market goal, like building demand, winning deals, delighting customers, and scaling growth

results.title: OpenAI's Agent Builder: Temporary Issues and Permanent Lockin | Dave Slutzkin posted on the topic | LinkedIn
results.content: OpenAI's new Agent Builder is bad. Some of that is temporary, some is permanent. Temporary things, most of which will be fixed in the next month or two: - The UI is not at all polished. It's clunky, as if it was built by codex without much supervision in 6 weeks. (It was.) - It forces you to drag and drop, but building agent workflows with prompts is the way a lot of people are going. - There's no visibility into each step in the process. Logging matters for agents - if it's not working, why not? - A bunch of the debugging is very manual and really only accessible to devs, so it's not a general-access solution yet. - The permissioning is weird, it can't possibly work in a big company. But all of these things will get fixed pretty soon, I'm sure. Once they've worked on it for 12 weeks - [...] AgentKit sucks. But that’s exactly what OpenAI wanted. I’ve been testing AgentKit for a few days → it’s not great. At first glance, it looks like a full workflow builder inside ChatGPT: - Agent Builder → visual canvas with versioning and chaining - Connector Registry → centralized control over which tools agents can access - Embedded ChatKit → agents get a real chat UI inside your product - Built-in evaluation & trace analysis → see and grade agent reasoning steps - Automated prompt optimization → refine prompts based on outcomes - Multi-model evaluation support → test agents across different models in one place It "sounds" like a serious automation layer. But when you actually use it → it SUCKS Here’s what using it feels like: 1. MCP fails half the time. 2. Agents don’t retry or re-ask [...] are minimal and opaque. 6. Recycled features - Much of this is repackaged from the Assistants API they're deprecating. (File search, vector stores, evaluations, these all existed before.) 7. Integration issues - MCP connections are buggy with significant setup friction. My Thoughts: Will it improve? Probably. Am I migrating my workflows? Absolutely not. Agent Builder isn't the automation killer the hype suggests. Established platforms remain more reliable, flexible, and transparent imo atleast.

The release targets a common pain point: fragmented AI agents operating without coordinated data. HubSpot said the tools address situations where, for example, a sales prospecting agent contacts a customer the same week a contact center service agent handles an open complaint from that account — with neither agent aware of the other.

Ignite Reading, a virtual literacy tutoring program operating across more than 25 states, built a custom agent that automatically finds and parses school district academic calendars. A task that previously took 15 to 20 minutes per district now takes seconds, saving more than 350 hours a year, according to HubSpot. [...] ### The Gist

 Unified agent management. All AI agents centrally managed with shared customer context.
 Natural language automation. Custom agents built using existing HubSpot customer data.
 Go-to-market team impact. Professional and enterprise teams gain improved visibility and efficiency.

results.title: HubSpot Agent Builder: What We Learned Building Custom Agents
results.content:
The limiting factors became things like:

 whether activity was associated with the Deal, Contact, or both
 whether the agent could access the actual content of a communication
 whether an internal process had a structured CRM property
 whether calls contained notes
 whether tasks were completed or merely left open
 whether information existed in one part of the CRM but not another

At that point, more prompt engineering was not the answer.

> The quality of a CRM agent is constrained by the quality, structure, associations, and accessibility of the CRM data it has to reason over.

That is probably the most important thing we learned from the experiment.

## Missing data does not always mean a broken process

This was another important correction we had to make. [...] It does mean an agent can expose something useful about your CRM architecture: which decisions repeatedly require humans to reconstruct the story from scattered activity instead of reading a clear current status.

In that sense, Agent Builder can function as a stress test for CRM design.

## Be careful with system properties and false patterns

We also ran into two less obvious issues that are worth mentioning.

First, an AI agent can misinterpret a CRM property if the property name sounds relevant but its actual HubSpot meaning is different. We had to explicitly tell the agent not to treat unrelated HubSpot system properties as proxies for a client’s loan-review process.

Second, you have to watch for selection bias. [...] ## What is HubSpot Agent Builder?

HubSpot Agent Builder is a beta tool inside Agent Hub for creating custom AI agents around your own business processes.

Instead of using a generic chatbot, you define the agent’s:

 Instructions: what it should do, how it should reason, and how it should format its output
 Actions: such as reading or writing HubSpot CRM records, browsing the web, or using other available tools
 Knowledge: persistent context such as knowledge vaults, brand information, products and services, or other business documentation
 Inputs: information supplied at runtime, including CRM objects or configurable values
